text: NASA’s Human Research Program has pinpointed five hazards that astronauts will encounter on their journeys. These include space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity (and the lack of it), and closed or hostile environments.
quote: These include space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity (and the lack of it), and closed or hostile environments.

text: These hazards do not stand alone. They can feed off one another and exacerbate effects on the human body.
quote: They can feed off one another and exacerbate effects on the human body

text: The hazards’ effects on the human body are being studied using ground-based analogs, laboratories, and the International Space Station.
quote: which are being studied using ground-based analogs, laboratories, and the International Space Station

text: Invisible to the human eye, space radiation is not only stealthy but considered one of the most hazardous aspects of spaceflight.
quote: Invisible to the human eye, space radiation is not only stealthy but considered one of the most hazardous aspects of spaceflight.

text: Behavioral responses occur among groups of people far from Earth who are isolated and confined in a small space over a long period of time.
quote: Behavioral responses occur among groups of people far from Earth who are isolated and confined in a small space over a long period of time.

text: Crews must be carefully chosen, trained, and supported to ensure they can work effectively as a team for months or years in space.
quote: Crews must be carefully chosen, trained, and supported to ensure they can work effectively as a team for months or years in space.

text: Instructions, new supplies, medical care, and more become increasingly challenging to receive from Earth as astronauts venture deeper into space.
quote: Instructions, new supplies, medical care, and more become increasingly challenging to receive from Earth as astronauts venture deeper into space.

text: Mars is, on average, 140 million miles from Earth.
quote: Mars is, on average, 140 million miles from Earth.

text: Rather than a three-day lunar trip, astronauts would be leaving our planet for roughly three years.
quote: Rather than a three-day lunar trip, astronauts would be leaving our planet for roughly three years.

text: Planning and self-sufficiency will be key to successful deep space missions.
quote: Planning and self-sufficiency will be key to successful deep space missions.

text: Astronauts' entire bodies – muscles, bones, inner ear, and organs – must adjust to the new gravities encountered on the space station or their spacecraft, as well as on the Moon, Mars, and Earth once they return home.
quote: Astronauts' entire bodies – muscles, bones, inner ear, and organs – must adjust to the new gravities encountered on the space station or their spacecraft

text: On Mars, astronauts would need to live and work in three-eighths of Earth’s gravitational pull for up to two years.
quote: On Mars, astronauts would need to live and work in three-eighths of Earth’s gravitational pull for up to two years.

text: Throughout this time, their bodies – muscles, bones, inner ear, and organs – will be adjusting to new gravitational loads.
quote: Throughout this time, their bodies – muscles, bones, inner ear, and organs – will be adjusting to new gravitational loads.

text: Maintaining a safe ecosystem inside a spacecraft presents unique challenges, from ensuring optimal temperatures, pressures, and lighting, to reducing noise, monitoring microbial communities, and tracking immune responses.
quote: from ensuring optimal temperatures, pressures, and lighting, to reducing noise, monitoring microbial communities, and tracking immune responses

text: A spacecraft is not only a home, it’s also a machine.
quote: A spacecraft is not only a home, it’s also a machine.

text: Important habitability factors include temperature, pressure, lighting, noise, the presence of microbes, and more.
quote: Important habitability factors include temperature, pressure, lighting, noise, the presence of microbes, and more.

text: The stresses of spaceflight can awaken inactive viruses inside the bodies of astronauts, leading to rashes and other symptoms. Ongoing work seeks to further understand changes in the immune system to better protect astronaut health.
quote: The stresses of spaceflight can awaken inactive viruses inside the bodies of astronauts, leading to rashes and other symptoms.

text: Astronauts can experience motion sickness, issues with hand-eye or gait coordination, and dizziness during gravitational changes, making it difficult to walk or operate a vehicle. Ongoing research seeks to help astronauts recover faster from these changes so they can perform tasks inside and outside spacecraft.
quote: Astronauts can experience motion sickness, issues with hand-eye or gait coordination, and dizziness during gravitational changes, making it difficult to walk or operate a vehicle.

text: Weightlessness alters blood circulation and how the heart and blood vessels function, potentially increasing the risk of cardiovascular events. Research focuses on minimizing these unhealthy changes.
quote: Weightlessness alters blood circulation and how the heart and blood vessels function, potentially increasing the risk of cardiovascular events.

text: Transitioning from a pressurized spacecraft to a lower-pressure spacesuit can cause health and mission complications when dissolved nitrogen starts to bubble within body tissues. Research focuses on developing better prevention and faster treatment options.
quote: Transitioning from a pressurized spacecraft to a lower-pressure spacesuit can cause health and mission complications when dissolved nitrogen starts to bubble within body tissues.

text: Skin and gut microbiomes can change in space, potentially increasing the risk of crew members getting sick. To help keep crews healthy, researchers are exploring these microbial ecosystems and how they evolve in space.
quote: Skin and gut microbiomes can change in space, potentially increasing the risk of crew members getting sick.

text: Astronauts on future deep space missions will take steps to avoid “the bends” during spacewalks, but following those steps also elevates the risk of mild hypoxia — a condition that occurs when oxygen levels in body tissues become lower than normal.
quote: mild hypoxia — a condition that occurs when oxygen levels in body tissues become lower than normal

text: A healthy, balanced diet is an essential element of crew health and performance. Ongoing research focuses on designing enjoyable, long-lasting, and nutritious meals for deep space missions and understanding the consequences of inadequate nutrition.
quote: A healthy, balanced diet is an essential element of crew health and performance.

text: Working in a spacesuit is challenging. In addition to cognitive fatigue and injury, crew members must also manage risks in the spacewalk environment, including decompression sickness, and low oxygen and high carbon dioxide levels. Research focuses on characterizing human performance in spacesuits and balancing pressure and oxygen levels.
quote: crew members must also manage risks in the spacewalk environment, including decompression sickness, and low oxygen and high carbon dioxide levels

text: All astronauts perform exercise during their mission to counteract losses in bone density, muscle strength, and heart and blood vessel performance. Researchers are studying what types of exercise will best protect their health and their ability to perform spacewalks.
quote: All astronauts perform exercise during their mission to counteract losses in bone density, muscle strength, and heart and blood vessel performance.

text: The structure of the eyes and brain can change with spaceflight.  Research focuses on understanding the long-term health consequences of these changes and preventing them from occurring.
quote: The structure of the eyes and brain can change with spaceflight.

text: Without gravity, bones break down and become more brittle, boosting the chances of painful breaks. Ongoing research seeks to better understand and quantify these losses, and help preserve bone strength through diet, exercise, and medication.
quote: Without gravity, bones break down and become more brittle, boosting the chances of painful breaks.

text: Isolation, radiation, distance from Earth, and other intense space stressors may all take a toll on the mental health of the crew. Ongoing research seeks to better understand and quantify these psychological risks.
quote: Isolation, radiation, distance from Earth, and other intense space stressors may all take a toll on the mental health of the crew.

text: Selecting a crew that works well together is essential for mission success and safety. Researchers are studying how to help teams in prolonged isolation and confinement function efficiently and quickly recover after setbacks occur. They’re also mapping the myriad risks from miscommunications and related team tensions.
quote: Selecting a crew that works well together is essential for mission success and safety.

text: Space crews experience multiple hazards simultaneously. Stressors include chronic sleep loss, constant work demands, and irregularities in their internal biological clocks. Understanding how to reduce the effects of these stressors on crew health and safety is an ongoing area of research.
quote: Stressors include chronic sleep loss, constant work demands, and irregularities in their internal biological clocks.

text: Future crews on deep space missions must be able to live and work in an environment where they may face unexpected problems with software, vehicles, or other systems. Research focuses on understanding when crews need information, the types and timing of required training, or other support options.
quote: they may face unexpected problems with software, vehicles, or other systems

text: During landing activities, crews risk getting injured. Understanding the likelihood of such injuries and how to better prevent them are areas of ongoing research.
quote: During landing activities, crews risk getting injured.

text: Crews exposed to radiation from space may be more likely to develop cancer. Identifying the best ways to mitigate this risk and understand what interventions may help are ongoing research priorities.
quote: Crews exposed to radiation from space may be more likely to develop cancer.
